curriculum.lesson_evidence: Passing and moving is a team strategy: after you pass, move into an open space so you can receive the ball again. This keeps the ball moving, makes defenders move and helps the team keep possession. Use clear communication ('Here!') and pass to open teammates, not just to friends. Keep the game safe with no contact, soft balls and enough space.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
A player passes the ball and then stands still. Describe what the player should do next and why.

FEEDBACK
They should move into an open space and call 'Here!' so they are available for the next pass. Moving after passing keeps the ball moving and gives teammates more options.

WATCH FOR
Thinking the person who passes has finished their job. Moving to a new space keeps them part of the play.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Set up a small passing game for 3 or 4 players (3 versus 1 works well). Practise 'pass and move' for 3 rounds. Record the longest run of passes and describe where players moved to get open.

Write a short reflection naming one choice you changed and why. Any movement is optional, adult-supervised and can be done in a gentler way or described instead.
